    ## Implementation Guidelines
    
    - Study nearby code before introducing a new abstraction or convention.
    - Keep changes focused on the requested behavior and preserve unrelated user
      changes in the working tree.
    - Follow existing TypeScript, React, and naming patterns.
    - Prefer existing shared components, hooks, utilities, and constants over
      duplicates.
    - Do not add dependencies unless the task genuinely requires one.
    - Comments that describe what the previous frontend (`mtrader-trade-ui`) did are
      load-bearing, not clutter. Most of them record a bug that was reproduced or
      deliberately not reproduced. Deleting one invites someone to restore the bug
      in the name of compatibility; keep them unless the behaviour they describe is
      gone.
    - Do not edit generated output such as `.react-router/types` or build
      artifacts directly.
    - Never commit secrets or real credentials. Document new environment variables
      in `.env.example`.
    
    ## Authentication and OTP
    
    `POST /v1/login` returns **HTTP 200 for every outcome**, including failure, and
    encodes the real result in the body (`status`, `isOtpEnabled`, `token`,
    `errorMessage`). Do not treat a resolved request as a successful login. The
    three cases are normalized in `app/api/mutations/useLogin.ts` into a
    `LoginOutcome` union; a rejected login throws `AuthRejectedError`
    (`app/lib/authError.ts`) so it stays distinguishable from network and timeout
    failures.
    
    When `isOtpEnabled` is true the login response carries an empty token; the
    session token is created only by `POST /v1/checkOtpCode`
    (`app/api/mutations/useCheckOtp.ts`). Never persist a token from the login
    response in that case.
    
    `status:false` together with `isOtpEnabled:true` does **not** mean the
    credentials were rejected: the server refused to send a new SMS because fewer
    than 120 seconds passed since the last one, and the code already on the user's
    phone may still be valid. That case still routes to `/otp`
    (`reusedPreviousCode`).
    
    The pending challenge lives in `app/lib/otpChallenge.ts`, in memory only. It
    holds the password because resending a code means calling `/v1/login` again —
    there is no dedicated resend endpoint. It must never be written to
    `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, or router state. A page reload therefore drops
    the challenge and `/otp` sends the user back to `/login`; that is intended.
    
    Code validity and the resend lock are the same 120-second server window
    (`OTP_WINDOW_MS`), so the screen needs only one countdown.
    
    ### Password reset
    
    Two endpoints, both in the server's `excludedMethods` list, so neither needs a
    token: `POST /v1/forgetPassword` and `POST /v1/resetPassword`. Both answer with
    `GuiStatusResponse` (`status` + `errorMessage`) and, like login, use HTTP 200
    for failure too — the mutations convert `status:false` into `AuthRejectedError`.
    
    The reset code never reaches the client. The server generates it, stores it and
    e-mails the operator a link built as
    `{hostname}/passwordReset/{username}/{token}` (`pkg/util/aws_client.go`). That
    string is why the route is `passwordReset/:username/:token` rather than the
    kebab-case used everywhere else: renaming the path or reordering the params
    breaks every link already sitting in an inbox.
    
    `ForgetPasswordRequest` has a `phone` field in the proto that the handler never
    reads (`GuiForgetPassword` uses only `userName` and `email`), so the client type
    omits it — do not add a phone input.
    
    Because the reset endpoint needs no session, the `_auth` layout deliberately
    skips its "already logged in" redirect for `/passwordReset/`; otherwise an
    operator with an open session would be bounced to the workspace and would burn
    a single-use link without being able to use it. A successful reset calls
    `clearStoredSessionState` (`app/lib/sessionLifecycle.ts`), the same browser-side
    teardown `clearSession` builds on: whatever session is left was opened with the
    old password, and the tab-scoped session layout must not follow the operator
    into the next login.
    
    ## Strategy Architecture
    
    All implemented strategy routes use
    `app/routes/strategies/StrategyWorkspace.tsx`. Strategy-specific behavior is
    primarily configured in `STRATEGY_WORKSPACE_CONFIGS` in
    `app/lib/strategyWorkspace.ts`.
    
    When adding or changing a strategy:
    
    1. Check `STRATEGY_WORKSPACE_CONFIGS` before creating strategy-specific
       workspace code.
    2. Keep panel availability, subscription keys, instrument selection, and
       command types config-driven where possible.
    3. Treat numeric `StrategyType` values in `app/types/index.ts` as wire
       protocol values. Do not renumber or casually change them.
    4. Confirm authorization, routing, subscriptions, and panel behavior together.
    
    Three conventions are shared by the tracker panels:
    
    - Inline setting columns (HFT `HftSettingCell`, and the shared
      `strategy/EditableStrategySettingCell` used by MAX_PRICE, MIN_PRICE and
      HFT_WARRANT) write through the same payload builder as the settings modal.
      Scaling and mutually exclusive field pairs must match the modal's encode
      function exactly; several wire fields are stored scaled (seconds ×10,
      milliseconds ×1000, percent ×10 or ×100), and a mismatch shows one value in
      the table and another in the modal. `EditableStrategySettingCell` takes an
      optional `confirmSave`, called with the **wire updates** rather than the draft
      text and before the optimistic patch, so a cancelled confirmation leaves
      neither a sent command nor a changed cell. Only HFT_WARRANT's price column
      passes one today (the price sanity gate); MAX_PRICE and MIN_PRICE have no
      absolute price field to check.
    - The order book panel renders its strategy actions (settings, start/stop, add
      position, cancel all) only through `StrategyControlsOverlay`, in the board's
      bottom-left corner. The panel toolbar carries view preferences alone: the
      `hasStrategyControls` / `isStrategyRunning` toolbar parameters that used to
      mirror those actions were removed on purpose, because a stop-strategy button
      ended up next to the view toggles an operator clicks by reflex. Add a
      strategy by passing the overlay its label prefix and handlers, not by adding
      another `isXStrategy` branch to the toolbar. The one non-view button there,
      "refresh order book data", is a deliberate exception: it only re-subscribes
      the depth feed, sends no order or strategy command, and is the operator's
      only way out of a silent freeze (see § The itch socket is shared). It sits
      after the panel's own buttons, not leftmost.
    - Strategy settings that are not in `WsStrategyResponseFields` arrive raw under
      `extraFields`; each strategy unwraps them with its own `get<X>Field` helper
      (`{}` means "default value", not zero). Send updates back through the same
      `create<X>Payload` builder the settings modal uses, keyed by wire field
      names, so the inline cell's optimistic patch lands on the same keys.
    - An optimistic patch is undone with `strategyDataStore.revertPatch`, never
      by patching the old fields back. The patch writes top level while the
      server keeps most settings under `extraFields`; merging the old fields
      left the new top-level key in place, the `get<X>Field` readers prefer top
      level, so a rejected edit stayed on screen and the next start/stop sent it
      to the engine (fixed 2026-10-16 in the shared inline cell, HFT, Varant and
      Varant Toplu). `revertPatch` touches only the patched keys, and only while
      they still hold the patched value, so a newer snapshot is not overwritten.
    - **Overlapping commands to one strategy are not coordinated, on purpose**
      (product decision 2026-10-21, see § Decisions and Boundaries). Every
      strategy command is a full payload, the engine applies concurrent
      commands in lock order rather than send order, and the echo replaces the
      whole snapshot entry. So two commands to the same strategy within one
      request's round trip — an edit while a stop is in flight, two inline
      edits of the same list, a settings modal saved while another path changed
      the strategy — can undo each other. All trackers (HFT, Tavan, Taban,
      Varant, Varant Toplu) accept this: the operator does not issue commands
      milliseconds apart, and the simple patch-after-reply path has run in
      production for a long time. A per-strategy command pipeline that closed
      these races (queue, separate optimistic layer, stop-dominates re-send,
      modal three-way merge) was built and then rolled back untested; it is kept
      on the local branch `archive/strategy-command-pipeline`. Do not add
      per-path fixes for these races; they belong to one general solution,
      ideally with backend support (a command id in the echo, or the engine
      applying a strategy's commands in arrival order).
    
    HFT_WARRANT nests derivative rows under an underlying row in a single
    `DataTable`. Two consequences: `DataTable` takes `enableRowSelection` so child
    rows stay out of bulk actions, and `PanelSubscription.derivativeInstrumentIds`
    carries the derivatives into the market subscription — that list comes from the
    live strategy snapshot (`Derivative_Orders`), not from the panel record.
    
    Both nested trackers (HFT_WARRANT and HFT_WARRANT_ADVANCED) expand an
    underlying row by a click on an empty part of the row (`DataTable`
    `onRowClick`); the separate expand column was removed on 2026-10-13. A chevron
    before the symbol only indicates the state. `onRowClick` ignores clicks on
    buttons, inputs, checkboxes and anything under `data-row-click="off"`, and
    clicks that bubble through React from a portal (the mini order book): keep
    new row controls interactive elements so they do not toggle the row. The
    symbol is a button on purpose — its double click opens the order book.
    
    HFT_WARRANT also carries two price scales in the same payload. `Criteria_Price`
    is raw in the **underlying's** scale — the engine compares it against the
    underlying's level price (`HftWarrant.cpp:475`) — while the `userPrice` of each
    derivative in `Derivative_Orders` is **decimal TL**, because the engine scales
    that one itself with a hardcoded ×1000 (`WARRANT_ENGINE_PRICE_SCALE`). Mixing
    them up sends an order 10× or 1000× off, so check which side of the payload a
    value belongs to before touching it. See **Price Scale** below.
    
    ### HFT chase type and its hidden fields
    
    `Hft_Type` 1 (Pozisyonlu) hides the no-position column; 2 (Pozisyonsuz)
    disables replace mode and passive chase. Hidden is **not** inert: the engine
    gates none of these fields on `hftType`. `isNoPositionMode()` is literally
    `startWithBuy || startWithSell` (`HftClassic.h`), `updatePosition` cancels every
    sell order at balance 0 when `startWithBuy` is set, `followMaxEntryLot` prefers
    `noPositionLot` over the base lot, and `sendAskOrder` arms a passive
    take-profit whenever `buyPassiveLevel` is non-zero. A strategy saved in
    no-position mode and then switched to positioned kept all of that until
    2026-09-28.
    
    `normalizeHftFields` is the one enforcement point — modal, bulk save, inline
    cell and order-book controls all pass through it. In positioned mode it writes
    `HFT_NO_POSITION_DEFAULTS` (the old frontend's reset values); in no-position
    mode it resets each start side's entry style/passive level when that side is
    off, and the stop loss when both are. The form hydrates the same way so a
    stale value never reappears on screen when the type is switched. Do not narrow
    this to "only on type change": old records already carry stale values.
    
    Stop loss "off" is sent as `Hft_Stop_Loss_Level: 0` by the form (as the old
    frontend did), while the engine treats only `-1` as off. This is known and
    unresolved; changing it alters live stop-loss behaviour and needs a decision.
    
    ### HFT_WARRANT_ADVANCED (Varant Toplu)
    
    Ported from the old GUI's `VarantTopluTrackerForm` (branch
    `follow_aggresive_momentum`). The engine lives on the `HftSrvProd` branch
    `hft_warrant_advanced` (`HftWarrantAdvancedCommand.cpp`,
    `HftWarrantAdvanced.cpp`); the attribute rows are
    `trade-data-app/scripts/sql/hft_warrant_advanced.sql`. Code:
    `app/components/dockview/warrant-bulk/`. It shares none of Varant's
    contract — do not reuse Varant's payload helpers for it. Like Varant, warrants
    are child rows of the underlying in one `DataTable`; columns are chosen so both
    row types fill them (Lot = send lot / quotation lot, Tur = limit / rounds done),
    and the table is dense (29 px rows). The density lives in
    `warrant-bulk/WarrantBulkDenseTable.tsx`, not in the shared
    `tableVirtualization.ts`: no other tracker uses it. A separate warrant pane was
    tried on 2026-10-01 and rejected by the operator. The mini order book on warrant
    rows (`WarrantBulkMiniBook.tsx`) and the dense table are Varant Toplu-only on
    purpose (product decision 2026-10-13); a flashing price cell on the underlying
    row was removed the same day — do not bring it back.
    
    - **No command before the settings snapshot.** The engine rebuilds the
      warrant list from every command; a start/stop, inline edit or bulk action
      sent while `strategyDataStore` has no entry sends `Warrant_List: []` and lot 0,
      which wipes the strategy. Every path goes through `getLoadedStrategyFields` /
      `splitLoadedRows`, and the inline editors are disabled until it loads. The
      settings modal is the one exception: there the operator supplies the whole
      list.
    - **`Warrant_List` is parsed by hand in the engine**
      (`parseJsonField`): a value ends at the first comma, an object at the first
      `}`. `encodeWarrantList` strips `",{}` from text fields and rounds
      `strikePrice` to two decimals like `warrantsToJson`, so a read-back does not
      drift.
    - **Per-warrant state comes from the account summary**, not from a balance
      message: `commandType 5` (`SUMMARY_<account>`), pushed by the engine at most
      once a second. `commandTypes` is `[1]` on purpose — `BalanceResponse.Profit`
      does not include warrant trades. Tracker and summary panel both request the
      summary for **all** spot accounts, so neither narrows the request
      `CommandSocket` replays on reconnect.
    - **The summary is not carried on table rows.** Until 2026-10 the tracker
      copied each strategy's summary into its row objects, so every account
      summary rebuilt the whole table. Now `getWarrantBulkRuntimeMap` caches the
      parsed rows and keeps a strategy's row object when its content did not
      change; cells subscribe to their own key (`useWarrantBulkRuntime`,
      `useWarrantBulkWarrantRuntime`), and the row colour ticks only when the set
      of strategies with a rejected warrant changes
      (`subscribeWarrantBulkRejectedChange`). The summary panel keeps its row
      array with `areFlatRowsEqual`, which works because of that identity.
    - **K/Z is summed in TL.** Each warrant's `pnl` is raw in that warrant's own
      scale; `sumWarrantBulkPnl` converts per instrument and returns `null` (shown
      as `-`) while an instrument is not yet in the store. `buyPrice` is in the
      warrant's scale, `underlyingAskAtBuy` / `underlyingBidAtBuy` in the
      underlying's.
    - **`quotationLotOp`** (`eq` / `le` / `ge`, per warrant) is the trigger
      condition: the amount eaten at the best ask compared to `quotationLot`.
      Files always arrive as `eq`; a missing value is read as `eq` on both sides.
      `le` fires on the first fill at the ask. `prevClose` was dropped from the
      list on 2026-10-01 (the engine never used it).
    - **Moment events** (buy/sell reject, per-warrant freeze) arrive as
      `Command_Type_HftWarrantDerivativeResponse` (`WarrantAdvancedEventCommand.cpp`),
      only to clients subscribed to that strategy. They bypass the command batch
      (`warrantBulkEvents.ts`) because two warrants can fire under one
      `unique_key` in the same tick; the tracker turns them into toasts, reject
      toasts stay until closed. Persistent state is still the summary's `state`.
      Two open trackers both receive the same event object; it is shown once by
      object identity (`WeakSet`), **not** by a shared toast id, which would let a
      second reject of the same warrant replace the first (§ Trading and Logging
      Rules). `socketStore` imports `warrantBulkEvents.ts`, so that module must
      not import the store or anything that does (`warrantBulkSummary` does).
      `Frozen` is the one exception: its toast has a per-warrant id, because the
      sell now moves between cost and +1 tick and a flickering underlying would
      otherwise stack warnings. Rejects keep separate toasts.
    - **The sell is at cost or at +1 tick, and it can go back.** The reference is
      the underlying price when the **buy was sent**: ask for a Call, bid for a
      Put (`HftWarrantAdvanced::underlyingMove`; a warrant of unknown type only
      follows the timeout). The sell moves to cost (`Frozen`, shown as "At Cost")
      when the underlying is adverse to the reference, when it is still at the
      reference after `Cost_Timeout_Ms`, or when it left the reference and came
      back; it returns to +1 (`Raised`) when the underlying moves in our favour.
      `Cost_Timeout_Ms` is milliseconds on the wire (`Long`, `0` = off) and
      **seconds** with three decimals on screen (`costTimeoutSecondsToMs` /
      `costTimeoutMsToSeconds`); both settings modals and the bulk save go through
      those two. The engine echoes it in the settings snapshot, so start/stop and
      inline edits keep it. The tracker has an inline-editable column for it,
      hidden by default (`WARRANT_BULK_DEFAULT_COLUMN_VISIBILITY`) and placed
      after Rounds even in a saved column order (`placeWarrantBulkColumnOrder`).
      An empty value is refused in the single modal and the inline cell (empty
      would send 0, which turns the rule off); in the bulk modal empty means
      "untouched". Any reference shown to the operator must follow the
      warrant type (`getUnderlyingReference`): showing the ask for a Put shows the
      wrong side.
    - **`Raised` and `ManualSellBlocked` show no toast of their own.** `Raised`
      is visible in the state column; it only dismisses that warrant's "At Cost"
      toast (same per-warrant id), so a cost warning on screen always means the
      warrant is at cost now (product decision 2026-10-16). `ManualSellBlocked` comes with the same
      rejection in the manual order's own gRPC response
      (`GUIManager::handleEnterOrder` → `FAILED_PRECONDITION`), which the order
      form already shows; a toast here would show one reject twice whenever a
      tracker is open.
    - **Order History's "Underlying Bid / Ask" column** comes from two more
      moment events, `BuySent` and `ReplaceSent`, which carry the order `token`
      and the underlying book at send time. `socketStore` records them into
      `orderSnapshotStore` (memory only, keyed by token) **before** publishing,
      so the column does not depend on a toast listener; the toast hook ignores
      both. The row is joined by `OrderToken`, which on a replace row is the
      **new** token (`NewReplaceOrderFromOuch`), so the event's token must be the
      same string as the OUCH token. The column exists only in this workspace
      (`getOrderHistoryColumnIds`): elsewhere it would be a default-on column of
      dashes in every order history. Inside it, a row that can never have a
      snapshot (free order, fill, cancel) is blank and `-` means "should have one,
      did not arrive" — keep that split. The engine does not replay these events:
      a reload, a dropped command socket, or no open tracker (the tracker owns the
      strategy subscription) leaves the cell at `-`.
    - **Position comes from the summary only.** No balance message is subscribed
      (`commandTypes: [1]`), and Varant's `parseWarrantBalance` is not this
      strategy's contract; a cell reading `useBalanceEntry` here reads nothing.
    - Shared badges (`WarrantBulkStateBadge`, `WarrantBulkStrategyStatus`,
      `QuotationLotOpToggle`) live in `WarrantBulkBadges.tsx`, not in
      `WarrantBulkCells.tsx`, so the summary panel and the settings modal do not
      pull the tracker's inline editors, mini book and itch subscription into
      their chunks.
    - **Call / Put badge** (`WarrantKindMark`): a square with one letter
      (Turkish A / S for alım / satım, English C / P), Call `up` green, Put
      `down` red, the tooltip is the type's name only (product decision 2026-10-16, which
      reversed a neutral letter-and-arrow version from the same day). On Order
      History's buy/sell-tinted rows it is `opaque`. On a tracker warrant row the
      badge **is** the mini book trigger and replaced its separate icon: do not
      put the icon back next to it, and keep the icon as the trigger only while
      the type is unknown, or the mini book becomes unreachable.
      `WarrantKindBadge` looks the type up in the summary, so Order History shows
      it only in this workspace (`showWarrantKind`).
    - **A warrant with an open position cannot leave the list** — the engine
      rebuilds the list from every command and would orphan its orders. The
      settings modal locks its remove button and blocks a file that drops it; the
      bulk settings modal blocks the save for that strategy
      (`findBatchOpenPositionConflicts`). The bulk modal does not subscribe to
      the summary, so it recomputes the conflicts from the current summary right
      before both save paths (direct and after the running-strategy
      confirmation); a buy that fills while the modal is open would otherwise
      slip through. A "remove anyway" confirmation was added
      and taken out again; keeping the lock is a product decision (2026-10-13).
    - **Bulk settings** (`WarrantBulkBatchSettingsModal`, logic in
      `warrant-bulk/warrantBulkBatch.ts`) open from the gear in the settings
      column header and act on **selected rows only**, like bulk start/stop and
      every other tracker (product decision 2026-10-13). The bulk strip above the
      table, which fell back to the whole panel without a selection, was removed
      the same day. The warrant table is shared with the single settings modal
      (`WarrantListEditor`).
      - Files are matched by the **underlying id the gateway returns**
        (`/v1/parseWarrantFile`, which already maps `AKBNK` to `AKBNK.E`), not by
        comparing symbol text. The request deliberately omits
        `underlyingInstrumentId`: with it, the gateway rejects a file whose
        underlying is not selected, and the operator could not reassign it.
      - Each warrant row has an underlying select. A file whose underlying is not
        selected arrives with an empty select, and the save is blocked until every
        such row is assigned or removed. If the same underlying is selected under
        two strategies (different account or identifier), its list goes to both
        (product decision).
      - `Warrant_List` is sent only to strategies that got at least one warrant.
        A strategy without a file keeps its list: an empty list would wipe it in
        the engine. A strategy with nothing changed gets no command, so the save
        does not stop it. Lot a
    ... command output truncated for persistence ...
     Do not "fix" either
      without a new decision. The first affects every primary surface: `Button`
      `primary`, the `Checkbox` tick, the `Tabs` indicator, the selected
      `TimeInput` value, react-select's selected option.
      Two more are below the text threshold and were ruled out of scope the same
      day: `muted-foreground` (≈4.0 in both themes) and `text-primary` on the light
      background (2.12). All four are pinned in `KNOWN_DEBT`.
    - A new token or a changed value must pass `npm run check:contrast`. Add the
      new pair to `PAIRS` in `scripts/check-contrast.mjs`; a pair that is knowingly
      below the threshold goes into `KNOWN_DEBT` pinned at its current ratio, with
      the reason. The script only reads `#hex` values, so define tokens that way.
    
    ### Icon buttons
    
    An icon-only button in or around a table — row actions, bulk header actions,
    column search, the inline editor's ✓/✗, filters, pagination, expand toggles —
    is `IconButton` (`app/components/ui/IconButton.tsx`). Do not hand-roll one with
    `p-1` or `h-6 w-6`: those boxes had no `shrink-0`, so a narrow column squeezed
    them to the icon's width and the buttons stopped being square and ran into
    each other.
    
    - The box is always square and never shrinks. Sizes are by role: `xs` (20)
      secondary controls inside a header cell, `sm` (24, default) row and header
      actions, `md` (26) next to an `xs` form control. The icon size follows the
      button size; pass the icon component (`icon={FaGear}`), not an element.
    - `tone` picks the colour from the theme tokens (`start`, `settings`,
      `confirm`, `danger`, `dismiss`, `muted`, `primary`, `neutral`).
      The `*Solid` tones (`confirmSolid`, `dangerSolid`, `warningSolid`,
      `settingsSolid`) add a resting background and border: without them the thin
      `Tb*` icons read as disabled in both themes. Their users are the inline
      editor's ✓/✗, the warrant settings modal's derivative delete, the
      Collective Orders row actions (product request, 2026-10-05: activate,
      deactivate, settings, delete) and the strategy Passive Orders row actions
      (fix, cancel; same request). `settingsSolid` rests neutral and turns yellow
      only on hover, because `action-settings` on the light background is known
      debt at 1.92. Do not switch the other bare `confirm` / `danger` / `settings`
      users (filters, tracker start/stop and settings columns) to them.
    - `label` is required and becomes both the accessible name and the tooltip.
      `description` replaces the tooltip text only — use it for "select rows
      first" or a validation error while the name stays.
    - `disabled` is soft (`aria-disabled`, click blocked, tooltip still shows);
      `busy` is the native `disabled` for an in-flight request.
    - Out of scope on purpose: the order-book overlays, FABs (`Button
    shape="circle"`), the sidebar and modal close buttons — different visual
      language. `DataTableHeaderActions` / `ColumnVisibilityButton` keep their own
      class (`headerActionButtonClass`) because callers pass the icon as an element.
    
    ### Badges
    
    A status pill — running/stopped, a warrant's phase, active/passive, a small
    count — is `Badge` (`app/components/ui/Badge.tsx`), or `BadgeButton` when a
    click changes the value in place (the warrant active/passive cells). Until
    2026-10 every panel wrote its own, and "running" came out in three paddings
    and font sizes.
    
    - `tone` is one of `running`, `positive`, `danger`, `warning`, `info`,
      `primary`, `muted`. `running` (`action-start`) and `positive` (`up`) are
      separate for the same reason as the tokens themselves.
    - Every badge has a border in its text colour (`border-current/50`, product
      request 2026-10-13): a soft tint alone did not separate it from a tinted
      row.
    - Two sizes: `sm` (default, 20 px including the border) and `xs` (18 px).
      `sm` fits the dense Varant Toplu tracker row
      (`WarrantBulkDenseTable`, 29 px); measure before growing it.
    - Pass the icon component (`icon={TbBan}`), not an element; `tooltip` adds a
      description, the visible text stays the accessible name.
    - `neutral` is for counts and tags that carry no meaning of their own (the
      passive-order row counts, the bulk-confirm field list).
    - `opaque` mixes the tint into `card` instead of leaving it translucent. Use
      it on rows that are themselves tinted: the Collective Orders rows are
      buy/sell coloured, a translucent badge melted into them, and that is why
      the status there used to be a raw-palette solid fill with white text. Do
      not bring the solid fill back; white text fails contrast on the dark
      theme's `action-start` and `warning`.
    - `ChangePercentBadge` stays separate: it is a numeric cell that inherits the
      table's font size. Coloured-text statuses (order side, VWAP state) and the
      Collective Orders row tints and side text are not badges and still use raw
      emerald classes there.
    
    ### Tooltips and accessible names
    
    `tooltipAttrs` (`app/lib/formControl.ts`) only writes `data-tooltip-*`; screen
    readers get nothing from it. For an icon-only button use `iconTooltipAttrs`,
    which also sets `aria-label`. `IconButton` with `nativeTooltip` writes a
    native `title` instead of `data-tooltip-*`; use it for a button that must keep
    its tooltip in a popped-out panel (the strategy Passive Orders row actions do).
    Never pass `title` alongside the default mode: the main window then shows two
    tooltips. Every tooltip opens after the same delay, `TOOLTIP_HOVER_DELAY_MS`
    (500 ms, product decision 2026-10-07), set on the `AppTooltip` and
    `AppCopyTooltip` instances; do not add `data-tooltip-delay-show` to a trigger.
    Native `title` tooltips keep the browser's own delay. Do not add `aria-label` to `tooltipAttrs` itself:
    many of its triggers have visible text (labels, symbol buttons, price cells) or
    carry a description rather than a name (a disabled reason, a validation
    error), and `aria-label` would replace their accessible name with the tooltip.
    
    The order-book overlays, FABs and the arbitrage passive-order row actions keep
    a native `title` next to their `aria-label` instead of `iconTooltipAttrs`: `AppTooltip`
    is mounted once in the main document, so its tooltips do not appear in a
    popped-out panel, while `title` does. Give such a button both, with the same
    text; the name is the action, and a disabled reason goes into `title` only.
    
    Text the operator may want to paste elsewhere (an order's reject reason in
    Order History) goes through `copyableTooltipAttrs`, which targets a second
    instance, `AppCopyTooltip`: `clickable`, selectable, with a copy button. Keep
    it separate — a clickable tooltip holds the pointer, and on the shared
    instance every icon button's tooltip would stay open over the control below
    it. Copy through `copyText` (`app/lib/clipboard.ts`), not
    `navigator.clipboard` directly: that API is undefined over plain HTTP, which
    some installations use on purpose.
    
    ### Enter to confirm
    
    `Modal` and `CompactModal` take `onConfirm`; Enter runs it through
    `useConfirmOnEnter` (`app/hooks/useConfirmOnEnter.ts`). Every strategy settings
    modal passes its Save handler there (product request, 2026-10-01, reversing the
    earlier "no Enter-to-save in settings" choice).
    
    - **The focused field is blurred first, and confirm runs a task later.** Number
      fields clamp, round and pad on blur (`settleNumberValue`) and `TimeInput`
      applies `min`/`max` there; a mouse click on Save blurs, Enter does not.
      Calling the handler directly would send a different value from the click path.
    - Pass `undefined` while a request is in flight and **while the inline
      `BulkSettingsConfirm` is open**: that layer lives inside the settings modal,
      not in the overlay stack, so only this keeps Enter from skipping its choice.
    - Do **not** pass `undefined` for a validation error when the handler already
      refuses an invalid form (`useZodForm.handleSubmit`). The error is often the
      unsettled draft itself (`1` typed into a `min: 10` field), which the blur
      above fixes; with the listener detached that blur never happens and Enter
      silently does nothing. HFT, ARBITRAGE, MAX_PRICE and MIN_PRICE lost Enter
      this way on 2026-10-01.
    - Modeless layers — `CompactModal`, `Modal backdrop="none"` and **every
      `draggable` `Modal`** — confirm (and `Modal` closes on Escape) only when
      focus is **inside** them, regardless of overlay order: the panels behind
      still take keystrokes, and an Enter in the send-order form must not confirm
      an open cancel dialog. A modeless `Modal` still gets initial focus and a
      `tabIndex={-1}` dialog so that holds. `draggable` counts whatever its
      `backdrop` says, because a draggable overlay is `pointer-events-none`: the
      `Add*StrategyModal`s and `WarrantSettingsModal` use `backdrop="transparent"`
      and, while they were treated as modal, an Enter typed into the UI behind
      saved them. Modeless also means no Tab trap, which matches a background the
      operator can click into anyway.
    - The order edit and cancel dialogs (`ReplaceOrderModal`, `CancelOrderModal`,
      `CancelPassiveOrderModal`) are modeless and draggable (product request,
      2026-10-01), so a second order can be targeted while one is open. Their
      callers give them a `key` per target: `ReplaceOrderModal` seeds its
      price/quantity draft only on mount, and without the remount the previous
      order's price would be sent to the new one. Keep the `key` when touching
      those call sites. `AddPositionModal` is modeless too; it stays mounted at
      four call sites, so it resets its own draft when the target strategy changes
      while open (`useDepsChanged`) instead of relying on a `key`. The cancel-all
      dialogs stay modal.
    - **Initial focus decides whether Enter reaches `onConfirm`.** A focused
      button consumes Enter (it clicks itself). Until 2026-10 every button-only
      confirm dialog focused its first footer button on open — "Cancel", or
      "Save layout" in `ConfirmBackToStrategyModal` — so Enter cancelled deletes,
      logout and the price sanity warning instead of confirming them, while
      "Cancel all" (first focus on its checkbox) confirmed. `pickInitialFocus`
      (`app/components/ui/dialogFocus.ts`) now sends focus to the first form field
      or, with none, to the dialog itself whenever `onConfirm` is set. Enter
      confirming every confirm dialog, the price sanity warning included, is a
      product decision (2026-10-07). Both `Modal` and `CompactModal` use it, and a
      modeless `CompactModal` now takes initial focus too: the arbitrage package
      form used to open with focus left in the table behind it. Because the
      dialog itself can hold focus, both Tab traps treat it as the boundary
      before the first element; without that, Shift+Tab escaped to the page
      behind the portal, where Enter clicked a background button.
    - Buttons, links, textareas, native selects, an open react-select menu and
      anything under `data-enter-confirm="off"` (the warrant derivative search box)
      keep their own Enter.
    
    ### CSS cascade layers
    
    Unlayered author CSS beats everything inside `@layer`, regardless of
    specificity. Tailwind emits its utilities in `@layer utilities`, so any
    unlayered third-party stylesheet silently overrides utility classes.
    
    - Import third-party CSS through its layered build when one exists, and give
      it its own layer in front of `theme`.
    - The layer order is pinned at the top of `app/global.css`
      (`@layer theme, base, components, utilities;`). Keep third-party layers
      before Tailwind's.
    - Symptom of a regression here: a component's own `text-*`, `font-*`, or size
      class stops applying. Mantine (removed 2026-09, see below) was the case that
      taught this: its reset `input, button, textarea, select { font: inherit }`
      stripped font utilities from form controls while it was unlayered.
    - When a shared rule in `@layer base` must not reach a third-party subtree,
      re-assert the exception with a class selector in the same layer.
    
    `TimeInput` (`app/components/ui/TimeInput.tsx`) replaced Mantine's
    `TimePicker`, the only Mantine component in use, which carried about a fifth of
    the initial load. Do not bring Mantine back for a single widget. The component
    keeps Mantine's keyboard contract (segment auto-advance, arrows, Home/End,
    `min`/`max` applied on blur); its list portals to the owner document's body
    unless `withinPortal={false}`, which inline editors that measure "outside
    click" against their own DOM need.
    
    ### Tables
    
    `app/components/ui/DataTable.tsx` owns the shared table shell.
    
    TanStack Table is v9, where features are registered explicitly.
    `app/components/ui/tableTypes.ts` holds the one feature set every table uses
    (`dataTableFeatures`) and re-exports `ColumnDef`, `Table`, `Row`, `SortFn` and
    `FilterFn` bound to it under their library names. Import those from there, not
    from `@tanstack/react-table` — the library versions take the feature set as
    an extra first type parameter.
    
    - An API missing from a table object means its feature is not registered;
      add it to `dataTableFeatures`, not to one call site.
    - `sortFn: "<name>"` and the default `"auto"` resolve only functions listed in
      `sortFns` there. An unregistered name silently falls back to `basic` (with a
      dev-only console warning), which quietly changes text sorting.
    - The pagination row model is registered for every table, so a table without
      the `pagination` prop runs with `manualPagination: true`; otherwise v9 would
      cut it to a default page of 10.
    - `RowSelectionState` is `Record<string, true>`: a deselected row is removed,
      never stored as `false`.
    - `getIsSomePageRowsSelected()` is true at full selection too; an indeterminate
      checkbox needs `&& !getIsAllPageRowsSelected()`.
    - A cell that needs more room than its column while it is open (the inline
      editor) asks for it with `useRequestColumnWidth`
      (`app/components/ui/columnWidthRequest.ts`). `DataTable` draws that column at
      `max(saved width, request)` until the request is released; the saved
      `columnSizing` is never touched. The cell finds its column through the
      `data-column-id` on its `<td>`. A `min-width` on the cell itself does nothing:
      the table is `table-fixed`, so the header decides the column width.
    - `virtualization.rowHeight` must not be below the real rendered row height
      (`strategy/tableVirtualization.ts`), and the virtualized scroll container
      keeps `overflow-anchor: none`. Until 2026-10 the button-carrying trackers
      (Tavan, Taban, Varant, Arbitraj) assumed 37 px while rows drew at 41: each
      window shift moved the content 18 px, the browser's scroll anchoring
      "corrected" `scrollTop` back across the block boundary, and rows jittered
      non-stop at certain scroll positions. Measure a row before changing a cell's
      height or the value.
    - Tracker rows show their state with a **background only** — no `ring` or
      border (product decision 2026-10-13). Tavan, Taban, Teorik, Varant and
      Varant Toplu used an inset ring on top of the tint (green while running,
      red/sky/amber/purple for live states); it was removed everywhere. The row
      colour helpers are the `*LiveState.ts` files and `warrantBulkRows.ts`.
    - A memoized cell must not compare `prev.row.getX()` with `next.row.getX()`:
      the row object is the same, so both read live state and always match. Pass
      the value as a prop (see the arbitrage `SelectionCell`).
    
    - Column visibility and ordering come from the `columnSettings` prop, not from
      a hand-rolled button. Omit the prop (or pass `false` / `enabled: false`) when
      a table's columns should not be user-editable.
    - Extra header controls go through `headerActions`; they render in one slim
      strip at the right edge, and the column-settings button always stays last.
    - `meta.control`, `meta.searchable`, and `meta.align` drive control columns,
      per-column search, and alignment. Prefer them over per-cell overrides.
    - TanStack re-sorts only when `data` or the sorting state changes, and it caches
      `accessorFn` results on the row object. A column that reads a live external
      store (change %, lot, profit) therefore sorts once and then freezes unless
      the table gets `sortStabilityMs`: `useLiveSortData` hands TanStack a fresh
      copy of `data` once per window while a sort is active. Without it, a live
      sort only moves when something unrelated happens to rebuild `data`.
    
    ## Internationalization
    
    All user-facing text must go through the existing `useT` translation system.
    Do not hard-code visible Turkish or English strings in components.
    
    When adding or changing copy:
    
    - update both `app/locales/tr/` and `app/locales/en/`;
    - keep translation keys and interpolation parameters aligned;
    - do not write `t("key") || "fallback"`: `t()` returns the **key itself** for a
      missing entry, so the fallback never runs and the screen shows the raw key
      instead. Add the key to both languages;
    - run `npm run check:i18n` — it fails on a missing key, a mismatched
      `{{param}}` set or an empty value in either language.
    
    A namespace is loaded in an effect, so a panel opened for the first time can
    show raw keys for a moment until its chunk arrives. That is accepted: holding
    the panel in a loading state was judged worse than the flash.
    
    ## Price Scale
    
    Wire prices are integers, and the scale is declared per instrument by
    `decimalCount` from `getInstruments`: the divider is `10 ** decimalCount`
    (`pkg/itch/instruments/instrument.go:144` in `trade-data-app`). In practice the
    field is only ever **2 or 3** — VIOP futures 2, equities 3 — so the divider is
    100 or 1000. It is not a display preference; it is the scale itself.
    
    - Never hardcode `1000`. Derive the divider from the instrument.
    - `app/lib/priceScale.ts` is the pure scale math (`getPriceScale`,
      `rawToDisplayPrice`, `displayToRawPrice`, `formatRawPrice`). It knows nothing
      about stores or React.
    - `app/lib/instrumentPriceScale.ts` is the bridge from an instrument id to that
      scale (`instrumentPriceDivider`, `formatInstrumentPrice`). It is a plain
      function, not a hook, because table sorting accessors call it too.
    - Amounts follow the same scale. The engine accumulates profit and open cost as
      `price × lot` (`Strategy::updatePosition`, `getOpenCost`), so there is no
      separate "amount scale". A consequence: **raw amounts from different
      instruments cannot be summed** — convert each to TL first, then total.
    - A form's prefill and its submit must use the same divider, or the operator
      sends a different price from the one on screen.
    
    Three places keep a fixed ×1000 **on purpose**, because they mirror a constant
    the engine itself hardcodes. Each carries a comment saying so; do not "fix"
    them:
    
    - `Theo_Price` — the engine sends `lastThPrc * 1000`
      (`ArbitrageTracker.cpp:2100`).
    - Warrant `userPrice` — the engine applies `userPrice * 1000`
      (`HftWarrant.cpp:579`). This is an engine-side bug for any warrant whose
      `decimalCount` is not 3, and it cannot be fixed from the frontend.
    - `Arb_Total_Profit` — a bespoke tick computation in the engine
      (`closeProfitTick`), not `price × lot`; its scale is unverified.
    
    Arbitrage compares two legs whose scales may differ, so both are normalised to a
    common ÷1000 reference (`toReferencePrice`), mirroring the engine's
    `undDecimalMultiplier` / `drvDecimalMultiplier` (`ArbitrageTracker.cpp:33-39`).
    
    FUND_TRACKER is the one module still outside this system: it deliberately
    carries `TL × 100` and `TL × 1000` side by side.
    
    ## Trading and Logging Rules
    
    - Import trading-side, transaction-type, and other wire constants from
      `app/lib/tradingConstants.ts`. Do not inline protocol magic numbers.
    - Use `createLogger` from `app/lib/logger.ts` for application logging. Know
      where it goes: console output is gated on `import.meta.env.DEV`, and there is
      no remote sink, so **in production a log call reaches nobody**. The only
      production signal is a user-visible notification. There are no
      `window.onerror` / `unhandledrejection` handlers either. A telemetry
      service (Mixpanel or similar) is planned; it will attach to the logger as a
      target, so keep routing errors through it rather than around it.
    - Do not call `console` or the toast library directly in application logic when
      the logger already supports the use case.
    - A `catch` around a request reports through `notifyApiError(error, fallback)`
      (`app/lib/notifyApiError.ts`), never `notifications.error(fallback)` alone.
      The fallback is shown only when nothing can be derived from the error, so
      non-request errors behave as before; a request failure keeps its reason
      (timeout, network, backend code) instead of a generic "operation failed".
      Where a flow throws its own `Error` with an already translated message, use
      `getStrategyCommandErrorMessage` (`app/lib/strategyCommands.ts`), which keeps
      that message but still translates an axios error.
    - Outage-class errors (timeout, network, bare 5xx, service unavailable) are
      deduplicated centrally in `notifyBackendError` by code: during an outage
      every open panel fails at once, and sonner shows only three toasts, so
      without it they pushed real order rejects off screen. Request-specific
      errors — order rejects, validation — are deliberately **not** deduplicated;
      do not give them a shared id. Order book panels fail together when the
      shared `ItchSocket` drops, so their notifications use one fixed id across all
      panels for the same reason.
    - Be conservative around order submission, cancellation, authentication,
      account selection, and strategy identifiers. Validate assumptions against
      the wire types and nearby flows.
    - **A timed-out order request may still have been executed.** The Axios client
      times out after 10 s (`api/client.ts`) and order, replace and "Add position"
      requests do not override it. Cancelling the request on the client does not
      cancel what the backend already accepted, yet the operator sees "the server
      did not respond in time, try again" and the button unlocks, so following the
      message can enter the order twice ("Add position" adds to the position). No
      frontend guard was added on purpose; the fix waits for the REST response to
      carry an explicit "order sent" confirmation, which needs the backend. Until
      then, do not add automatic retries to these calls, and do not treat a
      timeout as "not sent".
    
    ### A strategy's account is part of its identity
    
    The engine keys every order as
    `Account_OrderBookId_StrategyIdentifier_StrategyType` (`base_order.go`
    `NewUniqueKeyFromOuch`), and the order book's "has my order" markers come from
    that same key shape — both the itch subscription and `GuiGetOrdersFromLevel`
    build it from the single account the GUI sends.
    
    - Strategy identity is the account the strategy is **registered** with. Use it
      for `uniqueKey`, panel subscriptions, status/balance lookups and every strategy
      command. Substituting a derived account there subscribes to a strategy that
      does not exist, and the panel silently shows no status.
    - Only order **submission** may use a derived execution account
      (`accountForOrderBook`: futures orders must leave from the `DE-` account).
      Neither the GUI nor the backend validates that the two agree.
    - Non-arbitrage strategies register on non-`DE-` accounts
      (`isSpotStrategyAccount`), so their instrument lists must be spot
      (`instrumentStore.spotInstruments`). **These two change together** — allowing a
      futures instrument alongside a spot-only account filter creates a strategy that
      cannot place orders, and the error only surfaces at order time. Arbitrage is the
      inverse pair: `DE-` accounts, futures instruments.
    - The account → market mapping that actually decides this lives in the backend
      (`Users_Ouch` → `Ouchs.relatedMarket`, matched against the instrument's
      `relatedMarket`) and is **not** exposed by the accounts API. Until it is, the
      `DE-` prefix is the only signal the client has.
    
    ## Decisions and Boundaries
    
    Settled decisions, recorded so they are not mistaken for oversights. Change one
    only with a new decision from the product owner.
    
    Product facts:
    
    - Port 80 (plain HTTP) is open **on purpose**, so HSTS must not be added: it
      would break the installations that use HTTP. The consequence (credentials in
      clear text on an HTTP session) is known and accepted.
    - "Remember me" defaults to **on**; that is a product decision. The session
      token lives in Web Storage, not an httpOnly cookie.
    - Each machine is used by a single operator. Cross-user leakage through browser
      storage is not a practical scenario.
    - Orders filled while the connection was down are **not** announced on
      reconnect; operators track them in separate applications.
    
    Out of scope for this repository's work:
    
    - `.github/workflows/algo_gui.yaml` and `Dockerfile` belong to DevOps: deploy
      order, restart policy, per-customer rebuilds. Do not edit them. (For their
      information: `npm install --legacy-peer-deps` is no longer needed; `npm ci`
      resolves cleanly.)
    - Git history is **not** rewritten (`git filter-repo` and the like); it would
      break every clone.
    - Backend changes. Items that need one: the order confirmation above,
      half-open detection (ping/pong), telling a transient `Authorize` failure
      from a real session end, and the gateway's `subbedKeys` list, which grows on
      every strategy status request and is never deduplicated — the client can
      bound it by sending only keys it has not sent on the current connection.
      Varant Toplu (15) also needs the two gateway cases listed under
      § Strategy Architecture → HFT_WARRANT_ADVANCED to reach `development`.
    
    Accepted risks:
    
    - **Command races within one strategy** (2026-10-21). Overlapping full-payload
      commands to the same strategy (edit/stop/start/settings save sent before
      the previous one's reply) can undo each other; see § Strategy
      Architecture. Accepted because operators do not act milliseconds apart and
      a frontend-only fix touched every live command path without test time.
      Code review findings of this class (two in-flight commands, a stop and an
      edit crossing, a timed-out request applying late) are known; treat them as
      this decision, not as new bugs. Two related gaps are known and not
      millisecond races, left for the same future work: a Varant (HFT_WARRANT)
      start/stop or row edit sent before the settings snapshot loads sends an
      empty `Derivative_Orders` (Varant Toplu has the snapshot gate), and a
      settings modal kept open overwrites changes made meanwhile, including a
      warrant the engine deactivated after a buy reject.
    
    Declined, so do not start them unasked:
    
    - A test framework (vitest or similar). Plain-Node check scripts in `scripts/`
      are fine; they are not a test framework.
    - A CI check workflow. `.github/workflows/check.yml` (`npm ci`,
      `npm run check`, `npm run build` on every push) was added and removed again
      on 2026-09-28; the gates are run locally.
    - Restructuring: merging each strategy's code into one folder, shared column
      factories for MAX_PRICE/MIN_PRICE (they duplicate ~470 lines on purpose), a
      shared summary-view shell, splitting the tracker forms into hooks. Without
      tests every move is verified by hand only. If it is ever done, confirm first
      that dockview panel and component IDs come from strings rather than file
      paths, or saved layouts break.
    - More TypeScript strictness: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` (89 errors),
      `noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature` (160) and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`
      (247) were measured and judged not worth it. The five flags in `tsconfig.json`
      stay.
    - Upgrading `@types/node` past 22: it tracks the runtime major in `.nvmrc`.
      This is a standing decision, not a postponement.
    
    ## Verification
    
    Choose checks proportionate to the change:
    
    - Documentation-only change: inspect the diff and formatting.
    - TypeScript or React change: run `npm run typecheck`.
    - Style or convention-sensitive change: also run `npm run lint`.
    - Broad UI, routing, configuration, or dependency change: also run
      `npm run build`.
    - Formatting-heavy change: run `npm run format:check`.
    - Theme token or translation change: run `npm run check:contrast` or
      `npm run check:i18n`. `npm run check` runs all static gates together.
    
    If a relevant check cannot be run or fails for a pre-existing reason, report it
    clearly instead of claiming the change is fully verified.
    
    ## Documentation
    
    Keep `README.md`, `.env.example`, and this file aligned with meaningful changes
    to setup, commands, architecture, or contributor workflow. `README.md` describes
    what the product does and how to run it; this file describes what an agent must
    know before changing the code. Keep the strategy list in both in step.
    
    When a fix establishes an invariant that a future change could silently break,
    record the invariant **in this file**, next to the code area it protects, with
    the reason; a settled product decision goes to § Decisions and Boundaries.
    
    Code comments cite two older sources that are no longer in the repository:
    finding IDs such as `R3-04` come from the September 2026 revision report, and
    item numbers such as `2.28` from `docs/kalan-tasklar.md` (deleted in
    `79756bf7`; `git show 79756bf7^:docs/kalan-tasklar.md`). The comment itself
    carries the reasoning; the citation is only provenance.
    
    **Cite this file by section, not by line number.** Line references drift on the
    first edit and then point at unrelated text — four of the earlier citations in
    `kalan-tasklar.md` had already gone stale that way. Write
    `AGENTS.md § Section Name` (optionally `§ Section → Subsection`).

    import { useMemo, useState } from "react";
    import { useInstrumentStore } from "@/stores/instrumentStore";
    import { formatNumberWithDots } from "@/lib/helpers";
    import type { SelectOption } from "@/components/ui/Select";
    import type { ArbitrageTrackerRow } from "@/components/dockview/arbitrage/arbitrageTypes";
    import {
      getArbitrageSettingValue,
      type ArbitrageSettingsFields,
      type ArbitrageStrategyFieldKey,
    } from "@/components/dockview/arbitrage/arbitrageSettingsPayload";
    import type { BulkSaveMode } from "@/components/dockview/strategy/bulkSettings";
    import {
      DEFAULT_SETTINGS_FIELD_KEYS,
      getDefaultUnderlyingId,
      getInitialForm,
      toNumber,
      type ArbitrageSettingsSavePayload,
      type FormState,
    } from "./fields";
    import { useDepsChanged } from "@/hooks/useDepsChanged";
    
    interface UseArbitrageSettingsFormArgs {
      isOpen: boolean;
      mode: "single" | "bulk";
      row: ArbitrageTrackerRow | null;
      initialSettings?: ArbitrageSettingsFields;
      onSave: (payload: ArbitrageSettingsSavePayload) => Promise<void> | void;
    }
    
    /**
     * Arbitraj ayarlar formunun bütün durumunu ve değiştirme mantığını üstlenir:
     * form değerleri, değişmiş alanlar kümesi, seçili dayanak enstrüman, modal her
     * açıldığında değerleri yeniden besleyen effect ve kaydet/sıfırla handler'ları.
     * Modal kabuğu ile bölüm bileşenleri sunum katmanında kalıp yalnız buranın
     * döndürdüğünü okuyor.
     */
    export function useArbitrageSettingsForm({
      isOpen,
      mode,
      row,
      initialSettings,
      onSave,
    }: UseArbitrageSettingsFormArgs) {
      const [form, setForm] = useState<FormState>(() =>
        getInitialForm(initialSettings, mode),
      );
      const [dirtyFields, setDirtyFields] = useState<
        Set<ArbitrageStrategyFieldKey>
      >(() => new Set());
      const [selectedUnderlyingId, setSelectedUnderlyingId] = useState<
        number | null
      >(null);
    
      const instruments = useInstrumentStore((state) => state.instruments);
      const underlyingOptions = useMemo<SelectOption[]>(
        () =>
          instruments
            .filter(
              (instrument) =>
                instrument.financialProduct === 3 ||
                instrument.financialProduct === 5,
            )
            .map((instrument) => ({
              value: String(instrument.instrumentId),
              label: instrument.instrumentSymbol,
            })),
        [instruments],
      );
    
      // Form açılışta ve açıkken girdiler değişince yeniden doldurulur; render
      // sırasında (effect değil: modal önce eski değerlerle commit edilmiyor).
      // Kapalıyken `isOpen` bağımlılığı sayesinde bir sonraki açılış yine tetikler.
      const hydrationInputsChanged = useDepsChanged([
        initialSettings,
        isOpen,
        mode,
        row,
      ]);
      if (hydrationInputsChanged && isOpen) {
        const nextForm = getInitialForm(initialSettings, mode);
        setForm(nextForm);
        setDirtyFields(new Set());
        const initialUnderlying =
          mode === "single"
            ? toNumber(
                getArbitrageSettingValue(
                  initialSettings,
                  "Underlying_Instrument_Id",
                ),
                Number(row?.spotId ?? 0),
              )
            : null;
        setSelectedUnderlyingId(
          initialUnderlying || getDefaultUnderlyingId(row, mode),
        );
      }
    
      const updateField = <K extends keyof FormState>(
        key: K,
        value: FormState[K],
        dirtyKey: ArbitrageStrategyFieldKey = key as ArbitrageStrategyFieldKey,
      ) => {
        setForm((current) => ({ ...current, [key]: value }));
        setDirtyFields((current) => {
          const next = new Set(current);
          next.add(dirtyKey);
          return next;
        });
      };
    
      const updateFields = (
        updates: Partial<FormState>,
        dirtyKeys: ArbitrageStrategyFieldKey[],
      ) => {
        setForm((current) => ({ ...current, ...updates }));
        setDirtyFields((current) => {
          const next = new Set(current);
          dirtyKeys.forEach((key) => next.add(key));
          return next;
        });
      };
    
      const updateFormattedNumber = (key: keyof FormState, value: string) => {
        updateField(key, formatNumberWithDots(value) as never);
      };
    
      const selectedUnderlyingOption =
        selectedUnderlyingId === null
          ? null
          : (underlyingOptions.find(
              (option) => Number(option.value) === selectedUnderlyingId,
            ) ?? null);
    
      const handleSave = async (bulkMode: BulkSaveMode = "preserve-untouched") => {
        await onSave({
          values: {
            ...form,
            Funding_Cost: form.Funding_Cost === "" ? null : form.Funding_Cost,
            Adaptive_Spread_Level:
              form.Adaptive_Spread_Level === "" ? null : form.Adaptive_Spread_Level,
            Underlying_Instrument_Id: selectedUnderlyingId,
          },
          dirtyFields,
          selectedUnderlyingId,
          bulkMode,
        });
      };
    
      const handleResetToDefaults = () => {
        setForm(getInitialForm(undefined, mode));
        setSelectedUnderlyingId(getDefaultUnderlyingId(row, mode));
        setDirtyFields(new Set(DEFAULT_SETTINGS_FIELD_KEYS));
      };
    
      return {
        form,
        dirtyFields,
        setDirtyFields,
        selectedUnderlyingId,
        setSelectedUnderlyingId,
        underlyingOptions,
        selectedUnderlyingOption,
        updateField,
        updateFields,
        updateFormattedNumber,
        handleSave,
        handleResetToDefaults,
      };
    }

    }
    
    export function NumberInput({
      value,
      onChange,
      disabled,
      precision,
      tickSize,
      min,
      max,
      error,
      onBlur,
    }: {
      value: string;
      onChange: (value: string) => void;
      disabled?: boolean;
      /** En fazla kaç ondalık basamak; verilmezse sınırsız (varsayılan). */
      precision?: number;
      /** Verilirse yukarı/aşağı ok tuşları değeri bu kadar adımlar. */
      tickSize?: number;
      /**
       * Sayısal sınır. `min: 0` verilen alanlarda eksi işareti hiç yazılamaz ve
       * blur'da değer aralığa çekilir; şema yine de son sözü söyler.
       * Faiz/temettü/funding gibi işaretli alanlarda verilmez.
       */
      min?: number;
      max?: number;
      /** Doğrulama mesajı; doluyken kırmızı kenarlık ve mesaj gösterilir. */
      error?: string;
      onBlur?: () => void;
    }) {
      return (
        <Input
          type="number"
          size="xs"
          value={value}
          disabled={disabled}
          precision={precision ?? UNBOUNDED_PRECISION}
          tickSize={tickSize}
          min={min}
          max={max}
          error={error}
          onBlur={onBlur}
          onChange={(event) => onChange(event.target.value)}
          onWheel={(event) => event.currentTarget.blur()}
        />
      );
    }
    
    export function NativeSelect({
      value,
      onChange,
      options,
      placeholder,
    }: {
      value: number | null;
      onChange: (value: number | null) => void;
      options: { value: number; label: string }[];
      placeholder?: string;
    }) {
      const opts = options.map((option) => ({
        label: option.label,
        value: String(option.value),
      }));
      const selected =
        opts.find((option) => option.value === String(value)) ?? null;
    
      return (
        <Select
          size="xs"
          options={opts}
          value={selected}
          placeholder={placeholder}
          isSearchable={false}
          isClearable={false}
          menuPortalTarget={typeof document === "undefined" ? null : document.body}
          menuPosition="fixed"
          onChange={(option) => onChange(option ? Number(option.value) : null)}
        />
      );
    }

    import { formatNumberWithDots } from "@/lib/helpers";
    
    /**
     * Sayı girişi mantığının tek kaynağı: binlik ayracı, basamak sınırlı ondalık
     * giriş, tick adımı. `Input` bileşeni ve arbitraj ayar yardımcıları buradan
     * geçiyor ki ayrıştırma ve biçimlendirme her yerde aynı kalsın.
     *
     * Değer sözleşmesi: **ham** değer, binlik noktaları atılmış ve ondalık ayracı
     * virgül olan bir dize (tr-TR); **gösterim** değeri buna binlik noktalarını
     * ekliyor. Çağıranlar ham değeri `Number()` ile değil `parseRawNumber` ile okur.
     */
    
    /** Ham/kayıtlı değeri gösterime çevirir (binlik ayracı ekler). */
    export function formatNumberDisplay(value: string | number): string {
      return formatNumberWithDots(String(value ?? ""));
    }
    
    /**
     * Sayı → **ham** giriş dizesi (tr-TR ondalık virgül, binlik ayraç yok),
     * basamak sayısı olduğu gibi korunarak.

        // transition: the incoming command intends to start and we are currently
        // stopped. A half-open package (derivative leg filled, spot leg not, so
        // undExcQty == 0 while contractQty > 0) blocks the start, and no worker thread
        // is spawned. The throw is mapped to a gRPC FAILED_PRECONDITION (HTTP 400) by
        // StrategyManager::commandReceived so the GUI shows a proper message.
        //
        // Every command (start, stop, settings) takes the lock, so a stop can't slip
        // past a start that is still validating and then be overwritten by it.
        {
            std::scoped_lock<std::mutex> lock(ArbitragePackageMtx);
            if (arbitrageCommand != nullptr && arbitrageCommand->isStarted() && !isRunning()) {
                long effectiveMultiplier = underlyingMultiplier;
                if (arbitrageCommand->getArbitrage().optionalUnderlying) {
                    effectiveMultiplier = (long) arbitrageCommand->getArbitrage().underlyingMultiplier;
                }
                std::string reason;
                if (!arePackagesConsistent(effectiveMultiplier, reason)) {
                    LOG_ERROR("Packages are inconsistent, not starting strategy! " + reason);
                    logPackagesInfo(true);
                    throw StrategyStartException("Cannot start strategy: packages are inconsistent. " + reason);
                }
            }
    
            BaseStrategy<TradableInstrument, ArbitrageTrackerCommand>::setCommand(strategyCommand);
        }
    
        strategyParams.updateFromArbitrageCommand(*arbitrageCommand, params.strategyType);
        LOG_WARNING(strategyParams.to_string());
    
        if (commandPtr->getArbitrage().optionalUnderlying) {
            underlyingMultiplier = commandPtr->getArbitrage().underlyingMultiplier;
        }
    
        if (instrumentPtr == nullptr || (!Enumaration::isTwoFutures(commandPtr->getArbitrage().strategyType)
                                         && instrumentPtr->isDerivative())) {
            LOG_ERROR("Instrument is null or is derivative! Stopping strategy");
            return;
        }
    
        arbitrageTimeCounter = TimeUtility::instance().getCurrentTimeNanoSeconds();
        setCommandCalled = true;
    
        if (state.drvPos < 0) {
            LOG_ERROR("DrvPos: " + std::to_string(state.drvPos) +
        }
    
        virtual void setCommand(const BaseStrategyCommandPtr strategyCommand) override {
            std::scoped_lock lock(commandPtrMutex);
            commandPtr = std::dynamic_pointer_cast<CommandType>(strategyCommand);
            if(commandPtr->isStarted()) {
                start();
            }
            else {
                stop();
            }
    
            if (this->commandPtr == nullptr || getSettings() == nullptr) return;
            notifyStatusChange.notifyAllUsers(getSettings());
        }
    
        virtual void workAsyncron() override {
            try {
                beforePeriodicChecks();
                while(isRunning()) {
                    doPeriodicChecks();
                }
                afterPeriodicChecks();
            }
            catch(const std::exception& ex) {
                Logger::instance().logInfo("BaseStrategy::workAsyncron an exception occurred: " + std::string(ex.what()));
            }
            Logger::instance().logInfo("9999999 exitting from thread. ");
        }
    
        // A pooled strategy's doPeriodicChecks() must be non-blocking.
        void onPoolAssigned() override { beforePeriodicChecks(); }
        void processInWorker() override { doPeriodicChecks(); }
    
        virtual void subscribe(const Subscriber<BaseStrategyCommandPtr,moodycamel::ConcurrentQueue<BaseStrategyCommandPtr>>& subscriber) {
            notifyStatusChange.subscribe(const_cast<Subscriber<BaseStrategyCommandPtr,moodycamel::ConcurrentQueue<BaseStrategyCommandPtr>>*>(&subscriber));
        }

    ## İçerik
    
    Bu bölümdeki teknik yazım kuralları `bilgi-tabani/` içindir. İnsan rehberi `dersler/AGENTS.md` talimatlarını izler. Kullanıcı sanity Excel'leri kod/repo referansı içermez; teknik dayanaklar `bilgi-tabani/test-incelemeleri/` içinde saklanır. Dizin yerleşiminin giriş noktası kök `README.md` dosyasıdır.
    
    - **Agent için yaz.** Süsleme, motivasyon cümlesi, "bu bölümde şunu öğreneceksiniz" yok. Olgu, isim, yer.
    - **Tek konu, tek dosya.** Bir dosya bir soruyu cevaplar. 400 satırı geçiyorsa bölünmeli.

    - **Kod referansı ver.** `src/Strategy/HftClassic.cpp` gibi repo-göreli yol; gerekiyorsa sembol adı (`HftClassic::onHeaderChanged`). Satır numarası verme — hızlı eskiyor; sembol adı yeterli.
    - **Birim ve ölçek açık yazılır.** Fiyat raw mı TL mi, ×1000 mi, ms mi s mi — her wire alanında belirtilir. Bu sistemdeki en pahalı hatalar ölçek hatalarıdır.
    - **Prod farkı işaretlenir.** `development`'ta olup `master`'da olmayan davranış: `⚠ master'da yok (2026-10-22)`.

    ## Dosya adları
    
    Küçük harf, Türkçe karakter yok, kelimeler `-` ile: `emir-yasam-dongusu.md`. Her klasörün giriş noktası `README.md`.
    
    **İlgili alan:** Frontend ve motor.
    **Sanity karşılığı:** P06, P07, P33; TC-ARB-R04, TC-ARB-R08.
    
    ### Çift Vade'de ikinci bacak miktarı
    
    Motor Çift Vade türlerinde dayanak çarpanını başlangıçta `1` olarak kuruyor. Yeni arayüzün `getInitialForm` fonksiyonunda `Underlying_Multiplier` için varsayılan geri dönüş değeri `100`. Opsiyonel Ayarlar açık gönderildiğinde motorun `setCommand` akışı komuttaki çarpanı etkin çarpanın üstüne yazıyor.
    
    İkinci bacak miktarı, gerçekleşen ilk bacak miktarının bu çarpanla çarpılmasıyla hesaplanıyor. Dolayısıyla `100` değerinin uygulanması, 1 kontratlık ilk bacak için 100 kontratlık ikinci bacak oluşturabilir. Development'taki mevcut paket tutarlılık kontrolü, yeni/boş pozisyonda bu oranı genel olarak engellemiyor.
    
    Bu durum iki bacağın miktarlarının ayrışmasına ve amaçlanandan büyük ikinci bacak pozisyonuna neden olabilir. Farklı oranların ürün tarafından desteklenip desteklenmediği bu incelemede belirlenmedi.
    
    **Kod noktaları:** `arbitrageSettings/fields.ts` → `getInitialForm`; `ArbitrageTracker` kurucusu; `ArbitrageTracker::setCommand`, `sendUnderlyingOrder`.
    
    ### Dayanak seçiminin mevcut stratejiye uygulanması
    
    Yeni arayüz, tekil ayarda seçilen enstrümanı `Underlying_Instrument_Id` ile gönderiyor. Ancak mevcut motor stratejisinin `setCommand` akışı, oluşturulurken bağlanan dayanak nesnesini, `params.underlyingInstrumentId` değerini ve abonelikleri bu yeni kimliğe göre yeniden kurmuyor. İlk strateji oluşturma yolu farklıdır ve dayanağı `StrategyFactory::createStrategy` içinde seçer.
    
    Bu nedenle komutta/kayıtta görülen enstrüman kimliği ile mevcut stratejinin fiilen kullandığı dayanak ayrışabilir. Kullanıcı seçimin uygulandığını düşünürken piyasa verisi veya ikinci bacak emirleri önceki enstrüman üzerinden devam edebilir. Mevcut çiftte dayanak değişiminin desteklenen bir işlem olup olmadığı ayrıca ürün kapsamına bağlıdır.
    
    **Kod noktaları:** `useArbitrageSettingsForm::handleSave`; `buildArbitrageSettingsPayload`; `StrategyFactory::createStrategy`; `ArbitrageTracker` kurucusu ve `setCommand`; `BaseStrategy::setCommand`.
    
    ## 3. Spread Arbitraj'da Otomatik yön ve kademe alanlarının uyumsuzluğu
    
    **İlgili alan:** Frontend ve motor.
    **Sanity karşılığı:** P32, P15; TC-ARB-R01.
    
    Arayüz Otomatik yön seçeneğini `Fs_Arbitrage_Side=79` olarak sunuyor. Motorun yön enum'u ise yalnız `Above=65` ve `Below=66` değerlerini tanıyor. `checkOpenable`, gelen `79` değerini ayrıca ele almadan yön değişkenine atıyor; fiyat ve koşul kontrolleri bu tanımsız değerle farklı `if/else` dallarına giriyor.
    
    Ayrıca GUI Otomatik seçiliyken kademe girişlerini `Open_Tick` ve `Close_Tick` alanlarına bağlıyor. Gönderilen Spread komut türü `F` olarak kalıyor; motor bu türde `Fs_Open_Tick` ve `Fs_Close_Tick` alanlarını kullanıyor.
    
    Böylece kullanıcının seçtiği Otomatik davranış ile motorun yön/eşik hesabı arasında uyumsuzluk oluşuyor. Görünür alana girilen kademe, motorun işlemde kullandığı eşik olmayabilir; motor görünmeyen alanın mevcut veya varsayılan değerini kullanabilir. Yön seçimi ve emir fiyatı etkilenebilir. Koddan “her zaman alım yapar” veya “her zaman satım yapar” sonucu çıkarılmamıştır.
    
    **Kod noktaları:** `arbitrageSettings/fields.ts` → `SIDE_OPTIONS`; `ArbitrageSettingsModal` → `isAutomaticSide`; `SpreadFields`; `getArbitrageCommandTypeCode`; `Enumaration::ArbitrageSide`; `ArbitrageTracker::checkOpenable`, `checkParameters`, `calculateWantedPriceOpen/Close`, `openPosition`, `openPassivePosition`.
    
    ## 4. Başlangıç ve bitiş saatlerinin farklı dönüşümlerle karşılaştırılması
    
    **İlgili alan:** Motor ve çalışma ortamının saat dilimi.
    **Sanity karşılığı:** P19; TC-ARB-R02.
    
    GUI başlangıç/bitiş saatlerini gece yarısından itibaren saniye olarak gönderiyor. Motor `isOpenSession` içinde başlangıç saatinden 3 saat, Çift Vade türlerinde 3,5 saat çıkarıyor. Bitiş saatinde aynı dönüşüm yapılmıyor. Karşılaştırılan güncel saat `TimeUtility::calcSecondsFromMidnight` tarafından yerel saatle hesaplanıyor.
    
    Algo-Setup temel imajında `TZ=Europe/Istanbul` tanımlı. Çalışan container'ın gerçek saat dilimi bu incelemede okunmadı. Yerel saat İstanbul olduğunda bu başlangıç hesabı, stratejinin seçilen saatten önce işlem aramasına izin verebilir; emir gönderimi diğer seans ve strateji koşullarına da bağlıdır.
    
    Olası etki, kullanıcının belirlediği çalışma aralığı ile motorun uyguladığı aralığın ayrışmasıdır. Etkinin çalışan ortamda kaç saat olduğu container saatine bağlıdır.
    
    **Kod noktaları:** `buildArbitrageSettingsPayload` → `Start_Time`/`Stop_Time`; `ArbitrageTracker::isOpenSession`; `TimeUtility::calcSecondsFromMidnight`; Algo-Setup `MAProdEnv/Dockerfile`, `MAAlgoProd/Dockerfile`.
    
    ## 5. Temettü değerinin fiyat ve yön hesaplarında farklı ölçekle kullanılması
    
    **İlgili alan:** Motor hesapları ve frontend alanının birimi.
    **Sanity karşılığı:** P05; TC-ARB-R07.
    
    Motor, Faiz ve Çift Vade Faiz türlerinin emir fiyatı hesaplarında `Dividend_Prc` değerini `100`'e bölerek çıkarıyor. Yön/kârlılık değerlendirmesinde kullanılan `calculateDiffTick` ise aynı değeri doğrudan çıkarıyor. GUI alanında birim açıklaması bulunmuyor.
    
    Bu nedenle sıfırdan farklı temettüde, emir fiyatını kuran hesap ile yön değerlendirmesi aynı temettü düzeltmesini farklı büyüklükte uyguluyor. Bu fark, yön/kârlılık kararının emir fiyatıyla tutarsızlaşmasına neden olabilir. Sorun yalnız arayüzün göndermediği Oto-Spread türüyle sınırlı değildir; kullanılan faiz türlerinin hesap yollarında da görülüyor.
    
    **Kod noktaları:** `InterestFields` → `Dividend_Prc`; `ArbitrageTracker::calculateWantedPriceOpen`, `calculateWantedPriceClose`, `calculateDiffTick`.
    
    ## 6. Çift Vade Faiz türünde takip tablosunun alan seçimi
    
    **İlgili alan:** Frontend.
    **Sanity karşılığı:** P15; TC-ARB-R19.
    
    Yeni GUI'deki bazı takip tablosu yardımcıları yalnız `Çift Vade` türü için özel alan seçiyor. `Çift Vade Faiz` bu koşula dahil olmadığından diğer türlerin kullandığı dala düşüyor. Bu durum `ConditionalStrategyFieldCell` ve pasif spread renklendirmesinde kullanılan `getPassiveSpreadOpeningThreshold` içinde görülüyor.
    
    Tür için anlamlı olmayan bir kademe alanının okunması, tabloda ilgisiz/sıfır değer gösterilmesine veya renklendirmenin yanlış eşikle yapılmasına neden olabilir. Etkilenen sütunların kullanıcı ekranındaki somut sonucu henüz yeniden üretilmedi. Bu bulgu motorun arbitraj türlerini karıştırdığı anlamına gelmez.
    
    **Kod noktaları:** `ArbitrageTrackerCells.tsx` → `ConditionalStrategyFieldCell`, `getPassiveSpreadOpeningThreshold`.
    
    ## 7. Tatil dosyasının yıl kapsamı ve yüklenme biçimi
    
    **İlgili alan:** Operasyon ve motorun takvim verisi.

    Çalışan dosyanın da eski olması veya tarihlerin sonraki satırlarda bulunması durumunda bazı tatiller hesaba katılmaz. Bu, takas gecikmesiyle düzeltilen vadeye kalan gün hesabını ve ona bağlı teorik fiyat/faiz hesaplarını etkileyebilir. Üretimde güncel bir dosya kullanılıyorsa repo dosyasına dayanarak üretim hatası olduğu söylenemez.
